title: bls12-381-fixed-g1-invert-g2: Frobenius-orbit parallel rho in GT

claims.statement: For a uniform nonidentity P in BLS12-381 G1 and an independent uniform z in GT, the attack in proof.md returns Q=[a]Q0 in G2 with e(P,Q)=z under the pinned pairing convention, using at most 2^126.32 total target-group-operation equivalents (dense Fp12 multiplications, C=20,000). It computes g=e(P,Q0) and then solves z=g^a by parallel distinguished-point Pollard rho on orbits of the order-12 Frobenius automorphism of GT. A twisted-state 2^16-adding walk uses pre-twisted table entries, so each step is one dense Fp12 multiplication plus 8 Fp multiplications for the 12 one-coordinate class keys; 1.25 units per step are charged. Under the stated random-mapping heuristic, supported by toy experiments with an order-12 automorphism, the success probability is at least 0.39. The budget is 1.25*sqrt(2*N*ln(1/0.61)) useful steps on N=(r-1)/12+1 classes, times 1.03 for abandoned fruitless-cycle walks, plus additive setup, distinguished-point lag, storage and output costs below 2^-19 of the main term. Peak memory is at most 2^113 bytes; preprocessing is at most 2^27 units and is included; nonuniform advice is 0 bytes. This is a classical cold attack with no uncharged advice or quantum steps. It is generic accounting of known techniques, not a practical break.

experiments.purpose: Run the twisted-state parallel distinguished-point rho on orbits of an order-12 automorphism x->x^lam in a prime-order-l subgroup of F_q^*, with look-ahead and stuck-walk restarts. Count all steps and report mean steps relative to sqrt(pi*N/2) and the success rate within the claimed 1.25*k0 budget. Toy-scale evidence for the random-mapping heuristic and for the full sqrt(12) class speedup only.
